user.title: Which LibrePower instance?
user.description: Pick the LibrePower core installation this Powerwall belongs to.

connection_method.title: How should LibrePower connect?
connection_method.description: You have Teslemetry set up, so pairing is available - no Gateway password needed at any step, and it works even on Powerwall/Gateway firmware that has started rejecting local Gateway-password logins outright. Pairing needs a one-time physical confirmation (toggling a breaker) and, after that, runs entirely locally - Teslemetry is never touched again.

powerwall.title: Connect your Powerwall
powerwall.description:
This adapter talks to the Gateway directly over your local network. You only need the Gateway password printed on the Powerwall itself — no Tesla account required for telemetry.

Your Home Assistant host must be able to reach the Gateway. If 192.168.91.1 doesn't respond, you may need a static route or to join the Gateway's WiFi network.

Battery capacity and charge/discharge limits are entered here because pypowerwall has no way to read them from the device automatically — use your Powerwall's nameplate rating (13500 Wh per unit is standard).

Charge/discharge efficiency default to 0.90 if left as-is - a reasonable placeholder, not a measured value. Override only if you have a better manufacturer figure for your specific hardware.

pair_teslemetry.title: Which energy site?
pair_teslemetry.description: Pick the Teslemetry entry and energy site this Powerwall belongs to.

pair_confirm.title: Confirm on the Gateway
pair_confirm.description:
A pairing request for "{site_name}" has been sent. On the Gateway, toggle the DC isolator breaker off then back on to confirm this is really your equipment - Tesla requires this physical proof of presence. You have about 2 minutes from when the request was sent.

Once toggled, submit this form and LibrePower will check whether it's been confirmed.

pair_verified.title: Pairing confirmed
pair_verified.description: "{site_name}" is paired. Submit to look up the Gateway's identifier - this is a separate step from the confirmation check above, so a slow response here doesn't risk timing out the whole flow. You'll enter the Gateway's local network address yourself on the next screen.

pairing_battery_specs.title: Confirm connection details
pairing_battery_specs.description:
Pairing succeeded - no Gateway password needed from here on. Enter the Gateway's address on your local network (the same one you'd use for gateway-password mode).

Battery capacity and charge/discharge limits are entered here because pypowerwall has no way to read them from the device automatically — use your Powerwall's nameplate rating (13500 Wh per unit is standard).

Charge/discharge efficiency default to 0.90 if left as-is - a reasonable placeholder, not a measured value. Override only if you have a better manufacturer figure for your specific hardware.

reauth_confirm.title: Powerwall password changed
reauth_confirm.description: The Gateway is no longer accepting the stored password. Re-enter the password printed on the Powerwall.

error.invalid_gateway_password: The Gateway rejected that password. Check the sticker on the Powerwall — it's the full string, not just the last few characters.
error.gateway_unreachable: Couldn't reach the Gateway at that address. Check that Home Assistant has a network route to it.
error.pair_pending: Still not confirmed. Make sure you toggled the DC isolator breaker off then back on, then submit again - the confirmation window is short, so a fresh attempt may be needed if too much time has passed.
error.unknown: Unexpected error — check the Home Assistant logs.

abort.already_configured: This Powerwall is already registered with that LibrePower instance.
abort.core_not_configured: No LibrePower instance found. Install and set up the LibrePower core integration first, then add this one.
abort.teslemetry_site_unavailable: That Teslemetry energy site isn't available right now. Try again, or use the Gateway password instead.
abort.teslemetry_not_loaded: The Teslemetry integration isn't loaded anymore. Try again, or use the Gateway password instead.
abort.pair_register_failed: Could not register the pairing key with Teslemetry. Check the Home Assistant logs, or use the Gateway password instead.
abort.pair_din_failed: Pairing succeeded but the Gateway's identifier couldn't be read from Teslemetry. Check the Home Assistant logs, or use the Gateway password instead.
abort.pairing_unexpected_error: Something went wrong finishing pairing. Check the Home Assistant logs for 'librepower_powerwall' - the full error is logged there - or use the Gateway password instead.

init.title: Islanding safety gate
init.description:
Tuning for intentional grid disconnection ("strong" export curtailment) - not normal operation. LibrePower will refuse to island below the minimum SOC, or once today's time-islanded budget is used up, whichever comes first.

The minimum SOC is never allowed below your LibrePower core instance's own backup reserve setting, even if you enter a lower number here - islanding removes the grid as a backstop entirely, so it shouldn't be willing to go any lower than normal operation already requires.
